agree.reason: The specific $1.80 loss, the 14-county point and the offer of invoices make this more than the usual yearly complaint, but it never tells her chains are 20+ miles away, that two pharmacies will stop filling for her members, or gives a deadline for meeting, so she has little reason to act now.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the unsupported 'a third will close' claim and doesn't link the 9 closures to rates, but 'losing money on a fifth of its work' stretches a top-20-generics loss (possibly offset by brand drugs) to all plan work, and the PBM-disclosure ask and 'known for years' line were added without support.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are only repeated, never worked: there is no sense of total loss at the writer's pharmacy or across 38 stores, no closure rate from 9 in two years, and the 20-mile chain distance is never used.

right_comparison.reason: It shows what members lose if an independent closes in the 14 counties, but 'there isn't one' and 'go without their medicine' are asserted rather than tied to the 20-mile fact, and there is no trend of what follows if rates stay as they are.

qualification.reason: The hedge on why the nine closed is honest, but there's no checkable condition, such as two pharmacies stopping plan fills if the July 1 contract doesn't pay cost plus a fee, and no May 1 meeting date.

objections.reason: It deals partly with the 'plenty of chains' objection through the 14 counties and with the 'yearly complaint' objection through specific figures and invoices, but leaves out the 20-mile distance and the two pharmacies' plans to stop filling, which would answer both.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter that suits both the plan and the newspapers, though it uses placeholders instead of the alliance name and signer, and it asks for cost only instead of cost plus a fill fee.
